approved_translation: Do not expect gratitude from the powerful; better to withdraw from the ungrateful than to serve them in vain.
context_summary: The Bodhisatta was at one time born in the region of Himavanta as a white crane; now Brahmadatta was at that time reigning in Benares. Now it chanced that as a lion was eating meat a bone stuck in his throat. After a few days the prince's son said to his wife, "Let us go to my father's country." The Princess Labam's father gave them a quantity of camels and horses and rupees and servants; and they travelled in great state to the prince's country, where they lived happily. The prince always kept his bag, bowl, bed, and stick; only, as no one ever came to make war on him, he never needed to use the stick.
interpretation_boundaries: Keep animal characters naturalistic, not anthropomorphic
Focus on the moral lesson, avoid cultural stereotyping
Do not depict religious figures or deities literally
